transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-09-21
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (CSM), Jordan Lee (SE) — Littleriver: Marta Reyes (Head of Data), Tom Nguyen (Dir Eng), Priya Shah (Security)
Links shared: onboarding runbook (https://app.redwood.ai/onboarding/runbook.pdf), security deck (https://redwood.ai/security-deck), pricing spreadsheet (link shared after call)

Summary (auto): Quick kickoff to align on technical owners, compliance needs, pilot scope and timeline. Plan is to run a 4-week pilot Q4 focusing on chat & embeddings for patient triage flows; evaluate latency and cost targets.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you making time today. I'm Avery, I'm your AE on the Redwood side, and with me is Samir, our CSM, and Jordan, our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:12] Marta Reyes: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get this started.
[00:16] Tom Nguyen: Yeah, morning, thanks. We have Priya here for security stuff.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Hi everyone. I'll probably ask the hard questions.
[00:23] Avery Chen: Perfect, that's exactly why we invited you. Quick agenda, we'll run through what Littleriver is trying to accomplish, go over Redwood's deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private — touch on compliance/SSO, then next steps. Sound good?
[00:35] Tom Nguyen: Yep.

[02:05] Jordan Lee: (SE) I'll kick off with a quick architecture sketch. So Redwood provides the same API across modes — you can start on hosted to move fast, and then if you need predictable throughput and isolation you can move to Dedicated or Private. The runtime handles batching, KV cache, and we have quantization profiles for cost.
[02:28] Marta Reyes: When you say KV cache, is that something we configure or is it automatic?
[02:33] Jordan Lee: It's automatic by default; we surface toggles. For high-traffic prefixes you can pin caches, and in Dedicated we expose more tuning.

[04:10] Tom Nguyen: We're largely on OpenAI today for embeddings, with an in-house microservice for routing. Our primary constraints are HIPAA-ish data handling and latency under 300ms for the triage flow. Cost is— cost is big for us.
[04:28] Avery Chen: Got it. HIPAA adjacency and 300ms SLO. For latency, Dedicated or co-located Private tends to be best, but it depends on token sizes and request patterns. We can run a small benchmark during pilot to measure real latencies.

[05:50] Priya Shah: On the security side, we need SOC2 evidence, SAML/SSO, audit logs, and customer-managed keys ideally. Also data residency — some data must stay in-region.
[06:05] Samir Patel: Yes, we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS in Private. I can share our compliance pack after the call.
[06:18] Priya Shah: Also egress rules; our infra team will want to whitelist IPs.
[06:22] Jordan Lee: We'll document the VPC peering and egress expectations. For Dedicated we provide fixed egress endpoints; for Private on-prem we hand you the package.

[08:00] Marta Reyes: Pilot scope — we want embeddings for semantic search and a small chat flow for intake, nothing that stores PHI except ephemeral context. Timeline: target pilot start early November and finish mid-December. Is that realistic?
[08:18] Samir Patel: That timeline is reasonable. We typically do a 4–6 week pilot. We'll need access to sample prompts, traffic patterns, and a couple of key success criteria from you (latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on our eval set).
[08:35] Tom Nguyen: For success criteria: under 300ms p95 for triage single-turn queries, embedding recall > 85% on our test set, and total cost under a target (we'll share target numbers).

[10:12] Jordan Lee: For the pilot environment we'd provision a sandbox account, give you API keys, and optionally a Dedicated pool if you want to test that configuration — but Dedicated requires a commit. Alternatively we can run a hosted benchmark to approximate Dedicated performance.
[10:30] Marta Reyes: For the pilot we prefer to avoid a commitment; can you emulate Dedicated with hosted?
[10:34] Jordan Lee: We can run controlled load tests on hosted and pick model variants that are performance-optimized; it's not a perfect match but it offers good signals. We recommend running final benchmarks on Dedicated if you move forward.

[12:05] Priya Shah: Regarding PHI — you said data is stored in logs by default?
[12:10] Samir Patel: By default, hosted API retains logs for troubleshooting for a short window. For customers with stricter requirements we offer retention controls and log redaction; Dedicated and Private give full control over retention. We'll share specifics in the compliance pack.
[12:22] Priya Shah: Okay please include retention windows and whether we can disable retention entirely.

[14:15] Tom Nguyen: Networking — we have a locked VPC and strict subnet egress policies. Can Redwood's sandbox sit inside our VPC or do we need to open flows?
[14:27] Jordan Lee: For hosted sandbox, you'd open outbound to our endpoints and whitelist IP ranges; for Dedicated we can set up a VPC peering or Private link depending on cloud. For Private on-prem, you'd host yourself so no egress.
[14:42] Tom Nguyen: We need a clear network checklist.
[14:45] Jordan Lee: We'll send a network checklist and sample Terraform for peering.

[16:05] Marta Reyes: Can we talk models — are you curating open models or is Redwood providing proprietary models?
[16:12] Avery Chen: We curate open models and have verified performance profiles; customers often start with more capable open models and then tune quantization profiles. We can also recommend smaller quantized variants for cost.
[16:25] Marta Reyes: Any experience with hallucinations on triage? We need high precision for safety-critical intents.
[16:30] Jordan Lee: We recommend grounding prompts, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with embeddings + reranking, and model selection. We'll include suggested prompt templates in the runbook.

[18:00] Priya Shah: Re: compliance pack — is there an NDA or DPA we should sign before you share more detailed SOC artifacts?
[18:08] Samir Patel: We have a standard DPA and an additional security questionnaire we can sign. I'll attach those to the runbook email.

[20:00] Tom Nguyen: Who's our day-to-day contact for the pilot?
[20:05] Samir Patel: That'll be me — CSM. Jordan will be the SE for technical questions and Avery is the account lead for contracts.

[22:40] Marta Reyes: Ok let's run through immediate next steps so we're aligned.
[22:46] Avery Chen: Sure. Action items on our side: send onboarding runbook, security deck, and a draft pilot success criteria doc. Jordan will schedule a VPC deep dive to cover network/Terraform. Samir will create the pilot checklist. On your side, Priya will share compliance controls and Tom will share traffic samples and target cost numbers.
[23:12] Priya Shah: We'll compile the SOC artifacts and share a list by Friday.
[23:15] Tom Nguyen: I'll export a week of traffic patterns and a representative prompt set by EOD Thursday.

[25:00] Jordan Lee: Quick Q — for embeddings, what vector size and recall thresholds are you using today?
[25:06] Marta Reyes: We're on 1536 dimensions, Faiss index, recall baseline is about 82% on our internal eval. We want to hit 85+.
[25:15] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll baseline that in the pilot. We'll also try different index configs and small model embeddings for cost tradeoffs.

[28:00] Avery Chen: Anything else we should cover?
[28:05] Priya Shah: One more on KMS — you said customer-managed keys for Private. For Dedicated, is CMK supported?
[28:12] Samir Patel: For Dedicated in cloud regions we can support BYOK integrations in most cases — we'll confirm per-region availability.

[30:00] Marta Reyes: We have a question about rollout after pilot — what's the typical time to production if pilot is successful?
[30:06] Jordan Lee: If pilot is successful, timeline depends on whether you choose hosted or Dedicated. Hosted can go to production in days; Dedicated provisioning is typically weeks for reserved pools and networking. Private on-prem is longer due to ops install.

[33:20] Tom Nguyen: Budget question — do you have a trial credit or promotional pilot pricing?
[33:26] Avery Chen: We offer pilot credits for new customers, and we can do a short-term pricing arrangement for Dedicated evaluation. I'll include numbers in the pricing sheet.

[35:45] Samir Patel: I'll put together a single page "pilot plan" doc with milestones: access, baseline tests, evals, go/no-go.

[37:10] Marta Reyes: Sounds good. If there's anything we need from your side to make approvals faster, let us know.
[37:16] Priya Shah: We'll need the DPA and clarification on log retention to show legal/compliance.

[39:00] Avery Chen: We'll send the DPA, security deck, and runbook. Also we'll share a short checklist for CIO/compliance so you can accelerate approvals.

[41:30] Tom Nguyen: Great. For the VPC deep dive, can we do next Wednesday at 10am PT?
[41:36] Jordan Lee: That works for me, I'll send an invite and include a pre-call network questionnaire.

[43:00] Avery Chen: Thanks everyone — recap: Redwood sends runbook, security pack, pricing; Jordan schedules VPC deep dive; Samir sends pilot plan; customer shares traffic and SOC artifacts. We'll reconvene after the deep dive to finalize kickoff date for pilot.
[43:20] Marta Reyes: Thanks, talk soon.
[43:25] Priya Shah: Thanks all.
[43:28] Tom Nguyen: Bye.

(end of recording)
